intro: Oak Hill is a small unincorporated community in the interior of Manistee County, quiet farm and forest land without the resort development seen along the Lake Michigan shoreline. Mineral ownership here more often stayed intact through direct family inheritance, with oil and gas leasing history tied to Traverse Group and Michigan Basin formations rather than the Antrim Shale play further east.

sections.heading: Farm-family ownership around Oak Hill
paragraphs: A lot of the land near Oak Hill has been held by the same families for generations, and mineral interests tied to it commonly followed straightforward inheritance rather than the more complicated splits seen near the lakeshore. If you're not sure exactly what your family holds, the Manistee County register of deeds in the city of Manistee has the recorded chain.

sections.heading: What we need to evaluate an Oak Hill-area interest

faqs.question: Is Oak Hill part of the Antrim Shale trend?
faqs.answer: No, Manistee County sits outside the Antrim core. Any oil and gas history near Oak Hill ties more to Traverse Group and other Michigan Basin formations.

faqs.question: How do I find out what mineral interest my family holds near Oak Hill?
faqs.answer: Start with the Manistee County register of deeds in the city of Manistee and pull the deed or probate record showing the transfer of the interest to your family.

faqs.answer: It can carry some value tied to future leasing potential, but that's a more speculative situation than an interest with an active income history. We'll be upfront about which category your interest falls into.

faqs.question: How do I find the recorded chain of title for land near Oak Hill?
